root_cause.text: Missing error handling control flow in mlx5_ib_dev_res_srq_init() causes the function to unconditionally assign freed and error pointer SRQ objects to device resources after a failed ib_create_srq() call for s1, due to missing `goto unlock` statement in the error branch.
root_cause.evidence: The patch shows that when ib_create_srq() fails for s1, the code destroys s0 via ib_destroy_srq(s0) but then falls through to execute `devr->s0 = s0;` and `devr->s1 = s1;` unconditionally, assigning a freed pointer (s0) and an ERR_PTR (s1) to the device resources. The fix adds `goto unlock;` after ib_destroy_srq(s0) to skip these assignments, preventing the use-after-free and ERR_PTR dereference issues that occur in subsequent code paths (lock-free fast path checks, mlx5_ib_create_qp() dereferencing, and mlx5_ib_dev_res_cleanup() double-free).

intent_record.intent_summary: Fix lock leak in mlx5_ib_dev_res_srq_init by ensuring unlock is called when SRQ 1 creation fails.
intent_record.what: Added a `goto unlock;` statement in the error handling path after `ib_destroy_srq(s0)` when SRQ 1 creation fails during resource initialization.
intent_record.how: This change ensures that when SRQ 1 creation fails, the code properly jumps to the unlock label to release the lock that was acquired earlier in the function, preventing a lock leak. Without this goto, the function would continue executing or return without unlocking, leaving the lock held indefinitely.

The missing goto unlock statement means the function continues to assign freed/error pointers instead of exiting the critical section.

commit 20da44dfe8eff5b61685e394dec690a5d9dc36ce
Author: Leon Romanovsky <leon@kernel.org>
Date:   Fri Jul 23 14:39:51 2021 +0300

    RDMA/mlx5: Drop in-driver verbs object creations
    
    There is no real value in bypassing IB/core APIs for creating standard
    objects with standard types. The open-coded variant didn't have any

bic_trace_step.reason: The diff shows the refactoring of mlx5_ib_dev_res_init() to use IB/core APIs instead of in-driver verbs object creations. The vulnerability is in the s1 (second SRQ) creation error handling. When `ib_create_srq(devr->p0, &attr)` fails for s1, the code executes `goto error6;` which only contains `ib_destroy_srq(devr->s0);` followed by `err_create:` label. However, the critical issue is that there is NO `goto unlock` or equivalent control flow statement in the s1 error branch. The old code had `goto error5;` which would skip the s1 assignment, but the new code at line `devr->s1 = ib_create_srq(devr->p0, &attr);` followed by `if (IS_ERR(devr->s1)) { ret = PTR_ERR(devr->s1); goto error6; }` means if this fails, devr->s1 is left holding an error pointer (from IS_ERR check). The error6 label then destroys s0 but the function continues to error handling without properly cleaning up or preventing the error pointer from being used. The missing error handling means devr->s1 could remain as an error pointer that gets assigned to device resources, causing the vulnerability described in the root cause.
